The new sheet: the engine without compases

Implementation 03, Phase 3. The same passages of My library drawn three ways: today's sheet in the app (vexflow-v2), the research engine with compases, and the new engine, which has no compases, no tempo, no silencios and no puntillos. In the new engine both hands share one vertical line per moment, the room of a stretch comes from the notes that need it in either hand, and empty time is drawn short. The notes themselves (hands, figures, beam groups, clefs) come from the algorithm of Phase 2, so they can differ from today's sheet; please judge the look and the spacing here. The LLM writes the notes in Phase 4.

  1. 1. A busy right hand over a quiet left hand
  2. 2. Both hands together: one vertical line per moment
  3. 3. A pause where neither hand plays is drawn short
  4. 4. Beam groups in both hands, and a sign on every altered note
  5. 5. Grace notes
  6. 6. Clef changes and 8va
  7. 7. A grace note before a clef change keeps its clef
  8. 8. An armadura change inside a line
  9. The whole song

Spacing

1. A busy right hand over a quiet left hand

The right hand plays semicorcheas and the left hand one chord now and then. The stretch gets the room the right hand needs; each left-hand chord sits under the right-hand note it sounds with, and the left hand has blank space after it (no silencio, and the chord stays a negra).

Hips Don't Lie — Shakira, from 0:49 (columns f1240 to f1419). Reference figure: negra 400 ms, corchea 200 ms, semicorchea 100 ms.

2. Both hands together: one vertical line per moment

What sounds together is on one vertical line in both hands. Semicorcheas are closer together than corcheas, and corcheas closer than the half notes of the left hand, in proportion to their time (the measured spacing of printed editions).

7 Years — Lukas Graham, from 0:07 (columns f177 to f419). Reference figure: negra 1000 ms, corchea 500 ms, semicorchea 250 ms.

3. A pause where neither hand plays is drawn short

About 3 seconds pass with no new note in either hand (the redonda of the right hand still sounds). Up to a blanca the gap follows the measured spacing; the time beyond it keeps only 30 % of the width it would add, so the line does not fill with blank paper. The playback cursor will move faster over it.

Drivers License — Olivia Rodrigo, from 1:18 (columns f1960 to f2179). Reference figure: negra 833 ms, corchea 417 ms, semicorchea 208 ms.

4. Beam groups in both hands, and a sign on every altered note

Both hands play corcheas that start at different moments. Every onset of either hand gets its own vertical line, and the beams of each hand stay whole. There is no compás, so every note outside the armadura carries its sign each time (rule 1); after a Re becuadro, the next Re# of the same group prints its sostenido again (rule 7).

Poker Face — Lady Gaga, from 0:38 (columns f960 to f1099). Reference figure: negra 504 ms, corchea 252 ms, semicorchea 126 ms.

Elements

5. Grace notes

A grace note is drawn small just before its note and takes no vertical line of its own: the main note stays on the line of the moment it sounds.

Moonlight Shadow — Mike Oldfield, from 0:19 (columns f480 to f639). Reference figure: negra 467 ms, corchea 234 ms, semicorchea 117 ms.

6. Clef changes and 8va

The left hand changes clef inside the line (a small clef before the chord), and the right hand is under an 8va line. These clefs come from the algorithm's starting hands; the LLM decides hands and clefs in Phase 4.

AITANA - SUPERESTRELLA | PIANO TUTORIAL / COVER, from 0:01 (columns f30 to f219). Reference figure: negra 882 ms, corchea 441 ms, semicorchea 220 ms.

7. A grace note before a clef change keeps its clef

The right-hand grace chord sounds before the change to the bass clef, so it is written in the treble clef, then comes the small bass clef, then the main note.

Grace Kelly — Mika, from 2:00 (columns f3020 to f3119). Reference figure: negra 477 ms, corchea 239 ms, semicorchea 119 ms.

8. An armadura change inside a line

Sol mayor changes to Do mayor: a becuadro cancels the Fa# on both staves, with room around it so that it does not read as a sign of the next chord. The second drawing adds a thin double line before the change (not a compás line): which one reads better?

Grace Kelly — Mika, from 0:19 (columns f480 to f679). Reference figure: negra 477 ms, corchea 239 ms, semicorchea 119 ms.

The whole song

7 Years, the whole song

The new engine on a whole song: lines break where no beam group is cut, at the longest pause once a line is 80 % full, so that a segment that the LLM changes later moves the lines after it as little as possible. 15 lines, drawn in about 53 ms.
